title: Admit conditional ordinary BIT saving 0.003503 by late helper binding
body:
Conditionally admit ordinary BIT saving 0.003503, strictly above 0.0035, by nine actual deferred-input helper retirements. This is a BIT component theorem; a compatible funded Gaussian supplier and the complete multiplication outer assembly remain unproved. No whole kappa >= 0.0035 or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Each retired helper has no outgoing read in its old inverse prefix, which contains destination-only cleanup and exactly one H1. At its first common rank-seven read, bind the newly owned helper through the original ADD's actual inverse matching map to the current main receiver. The old ADD then makes that whole receiver zero, so its H7 query is omitted. The runtime uses a literal ordinary COPY; the inverse counterfactual entrance is only a correctness proof parameter. Endpoint autonomy preserves every retained original input/output. Chronological first-read order makes all nine bindings causal.

Every lost H8 helper target is debited. Against ai-nanachi PR5512, combined with the retained earlier partial retirements, snapshots and paid refinements, the complete eighteen-call inventory is delta P=-540H1-378H3+306H4-162H7, delta T=-72H4-162H8. There are 11004 independent originals and 49 owned local arrays, separately reserved for simultaneous instances. The complete moment gain is 378(1+3^(1-C)-4^(1-C))+162(1+7^(1-C)-8^(1-C)). No copied value receives productive credit.

Rank-mass tail dominance proves convexity of the old complete moment. Elementary rational logarithm bounds then prove a strict new test at C=0.003504, without a numerical root evaluation. All productive debits are retained in both higher-moment contractions. Fresh finite product, batching, coefficient/prime, 49-array reserve, cover and acyclic ordinary-backend parameters give B=0.003503. The native arbitrary-function/all-column, complete ROW/spectator, constructive mixed-target compiler, ordinary cover/backends, precision, fixed-tape and analytic framework assumptions remain inherited premises, not independently verified here.

Gaussian companions provide a complete changed D25 provider at its old price p8, with the actual selected-to-ordinary receiver block Kz and exact caller composition; a full dimension-coframe specialization of the original free-group source with complementary main normalizers and actual helper endpoint grades; and signed/block deferred-input algorithms. Their isolated or illustrative savings are not a funded actual Gaussian cohort. The newer coupled-provider histogram is not substituted for the original universal-word source.

Adds eleven mathematical Markdown documents, including the retained four-retirement and SOURCE-fusion/refinement proofs so the construction chain is reviewable in one place. Proofs are informal and separately reviewed by workers. No mathematical computation, numerical pricing, source replay, solver, Lean run, web search or remote PR refresh was performed. Offline source pin: 5e0052ca0aa3036a3afa8b0438927377c8d97d53. Old interval and certificate statements are predecessor evidence. Publication byte checks are separate from mathematical evidence.

Start with bit.md's nine cut rows and causal deferred-input theorem, then analytic-funding.md and assembly.md. consumer.md spells out the multi-helper and exact matching argument. This result closes the requested BIT component threshold within its conditional framework; Gaussian funding and whole multiplication kappa are still open.
